lines.text: You can take off the hat, scarf and gloves {WHEN}. || The coat stays. Let's not get carried away.
{G} can come off {WHEN}. {WHEN2} you'll want {GP} back, plus an extra layer. || A round trip for {GP}. The evening brings a friend.
{G} can come off {WHEN}. {WHEN2} you'll want {GP} back, plus an extra layer. || Evenings look warmer from inside. I go by numbers.
There's a short shower {WHENP}. Have the umbrella with you. || Short showers are the ones nobody takes an umbrella for.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || Hours of carrying for minutes of use. Still the better deal.
Expect a shower {WHENP}. The umbrella's worth taking. || Ten wet minutes, then everyone acts like nothing happened.
Rain {WHENP} is possible but not likely. The umbrella's up to you. || I said 'not likely'. If it rains, I said 'possible'.
It might rain {WHENP}, so an umbrella wouldn't hurt. || Low odds. I'd take that bet, but I never leave the room.
It rains all day, so bring the umbrella. || The kind of day you put the lights on at noon.
It's raining all day. Bring the umbrella. || Every shop doorway has a puddle of other people's umbrellas.
The rain eases off later, but bring the umbrella for now. || Then the whole street shakes out its umbrellas at once.
Take the umbrella for now. The rain stops {WHENSTOP}. || Then everything's wet and shiny and acts innocent.
The rain stops {WHENSTOP}, but you'll want the umbrella before that. || After that, I'm out of bad news for today.
The rain stops later, but you'll want the umbrella for now. || Save the outdoor bits for after. I would, if I had any.
The rain stops for a bit, then it's back {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella. || I saw round two coming. It's my one job.
It rains, stops, and starts again {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella. || The dry bit is when everyone runs errands at once.
Later the rain takes a break, but it's back {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella. || The puddles won't even get a chance to shrink.
The rain pauses later, but it's back {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella. || Weather like this is why rooms were invented.
Snow starts {WHENP}. || Five centimetres and everyone forgets how to drive.
There's snow on the way {WHENP}. || The first hour it's magic. After that, it's logistics.
Snow moves in {WHENP}. || The one forecast that makes adults text each other in capitals.
It stops snowing {WHENSTOP}. || Then it sits there looking perfect until the first footprint.
The snow stops for a while later, then comes back {WHENP}. || Long enough to clear the path. Not to keep it clear.
The hat, scarf and gloves can come off {WHEN}. || Your ears can hear people again. Not always an improvement.
The hat, scarf and gloves can come off {WHEN}. || A very modest striptease. The coat stays on, thank goodness.
{WHEN} you won't need the hat, scarf and gloves any more. || That's as much good news as winter is allowed to give.
It warms up {WHEN}, so the winter coat can come off. || There's no chair in the world built for a winter coat.
The winter coat can come off {WHEN}. || Suddenly you remember you have a shape.
A shower comes through {WHENP}, so take the umbrella. || Everyone without one is in a shop, pretending to browse.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || Not enough rain to fill a puddle. Plenty to fill a shoe.
Expect a shower {WHENP}. The umbrella's worth taking. || With an umbrella it's weather. Without one, it's a story.
{WHENP} there's a shower, so the umbrella comes along. || Brief, wet, and gone. The perfect guest.
Pack the umbrella. Rain sets in {WHENP} and doesn't let up. || After that it's indoor weather. I've had it all my life.
{WHENP} the rain sets in for good. Bring the umbrella. || From then on, puddles are permanent until further notice.
There's a chance of rain {WHENP}. An umbrella wouldn't hurt. || The small umbrella exists for exactly this forecast.
Rain {WHENP} is possible but not likely. The umbrella is up to you. || I'd say 'probably not'. I'm good at 'probably'.
It might rain {WHENP}, so an umbrella wouldn't hurt. || The only gamble where losing just means wet shoes.
Rain is possible {WHENP}, so maybe take the umbrella. || I've done my bit. Now it's you versus the clouds.
It rains all day, so bring the umbrella. || Today the bottom of every trouser leg belongs to the rain.
The rain lasts all day, so keep the umbrella with you. || Every bus smells of wet coat today. Every single one.
Take the umbrella for now. The rain stops later. || Then the birds start up again, as if they were never bothered.
It keeps raining for a while, then stops. Take the umbrella. || The sky looks sorry afterwards. It never apologises.
It rains, stops for a bit, and starts again {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella. || It's not done. It just forgot something.
Rain for now, a break, then more {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella. || Rain that leaves and comes back. I'd have more pride.
The rain pauses later but picks up again {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella. || A rainy day with a tea break. Union rules.
{WHENP} it starts to snow. || Every sledge in the neighbourhood just got its hopes up.
Snow starts {WHENP}. || The first flake gets all the attention. The thousandth gets none.
The snow doesn't stop today. || Everything outside is the same shape now. A lump.
It won't stop snowing today. || The novelty lasts an hour. The snow lasts all day.
The snow stops later. || Then the snowmen start appearing. Some of them are quite bad.
It's snowing now, but it stops later. || Then it goes from 'magical' to 'still here?' in about a day.
It stops snowing later. || After that, the snow has nothing to do but get in the way.
Later on the snow stops. || Then every car wears a white hat for a few days.
Snow for now, then a break, then more snow {WHENP}. || A second coat. Winter's thorough, I'll give it that.
The snow pauses later and starts again {WHENP}. || I like a forecast with structure. Beginning, middle, more snow.
It snows for now, takes a break, and starts again {WHENP}. || The break is mainly so the gritters can feel useful.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP} and starts again {WHENP}. || Just enough of a gap to see the mess. Then it's covered up.
